lines: Every night, for six years, a mother lit a lamp in the same window.
Her son had marched north with the legions.
Rome sent no letters. No news. Nothing at all.
The neighbours whispered that she was wasting good oil.
But the baker downstairs always slipped her a little extra... and never said a word.
Then one night, the oil ran out.
And she wept... because she was sure it was a sign.
But down in the dark street, a tired soldier stopped,
and looked up at the only window with no light in it.
He knew exactly which one it was.
He had followed that light home, for three hundred miles.

lines.say: You can let it go out now. I'm home.

lines: Some lights never really go out.
